subject: EU-only processing — operator access & SCCs clarification
messages:
From: Compliance Team <compliance@pharmasys.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 May 2028 14:12:00 +0100
Subject: EU-only processing and SCCs — operator access and KMS?

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo last week. PharmaSys is moving toward a strict EU-only processing requirement for the workload we discussed. Before we progress to procurement we need: 

- A short attestation that processing (inference and any transient logs/metadata) can be restricted to EU regions only (we prefer eu-west-1).
- Clarification on SCCs: do you rely on the standard EU SCCs (controller->processor) as-is, or do we need an addendum for operator access controls / subprocessor list updates?
- Details on operator (Redwood) access: what triggers are there for manual operator access, how is access provisioned, and are all operator sessions logged/audited?
- KMS: where are keys stored (Redwood-managed vs customer-managed KMS), and will backups or snapshots ever be exported outside EU?
- Retention & deletion: what happens to backups, caches, and KV cache after a deletion request? Confirm max time to irreversibly delete customer content.

Can you provide any attestation/documents or a short implementation plan by next Wednesday (2028-05-10)? If needed, we can put legal on a call.

Best,
PharmaSys Compliance
compliance@pharmasys.com

Subject: Re: EU-only processing and SCCs — operator access and KMS?

Hi — thanks for the clear list. Quick acknowledgement: we can support an EU-only processing commitment for the hosted/dedicated options you evaluated; details depend on the deployment mode you pick (hosted with in-region isolation vs. Dedicated/Private).

High-level answers up front:
- EU-only processing: yes, we support processing in a pinned EU region and can restrict model execution + transient caches to that region.
- SCCs: we operate under the EU Commission SCCs for controller-processor relationships. For operator access controls, we have an implementation plan and audit evidence that we can share.
- Operator access: limited, break-glass + approval flow, logged to immutable audit logs that are included in evidence bundles.
- KMS: we offer both Redwood-managed EU KMS and customer-managed KMS (Bring Your Own Key). Customer-managed keys remain in the customer's EU KMS region unless you choose otherwise.
- Retention & deletion: typical backup retention is 30 days by default; we have an accelerated deletion workflow to remove live data and purge backups within a defined SLA — I'll include the full timelines in the implementation plan.

Naomi (cc) — can you confirm the specifics on operator session logs, backup handling, and the timeline we can commit to for complete purging?

We will assemble a short implementation plan + operator access matrix and share by EOD tomorrow. If legal/your privacy team prefers a call, Jordan can coordinate.

Regards,
Mina Haddad

Subject: Re: EU-only processing and SCCs — operator access and KMS?

Hi all,

Following Mina's note, a few concrete technical points so you have something you can share with legal/infosec: 

- Region & control plane: Customer inference workloads run in the chosen EU region (we typically use eu-west-1). The control plane that handles orchestration (metadata, billing) is able to be placed in EU for Private deployments; for hosted deployments we provide region guarantees and policy-based routing.

- Operator access: operator actions that require data-plane keys or decryption are gated by a break-glass flow which requires at least two approvers (on-call SRE + security reviewer) and is logged. Operator sessions are captured in our audit logs (session start/end, commands executed, justification text). Audit logs are forwarded to an immutable S3 bucket in the EU and can be included in evidence bundles for customers.

- KMS & backups: if you choose customer-managed KMS, keys remain in your EU KMS (we never export them). Backups and snapshots for hosted instances are stored in-region by default. Offsite/DR replication is optional and can be configured to remain within EU; we will not replicate outside the EU unless explicitly requested in writing.

- Deletion workflow: upon a deletion request we run a three-step purge: 1) remove active objects and cached prefixes; 2) rotate and zeroize ephemeral KV caches; 3) schedule backup snapshot expiration and cryptographic destruction. Standard backup retention is 30 days; we can offer a reduced retention SLA for enterprise customers (example: 7-day retention with 14-day SLA to crypto-erase backups). We will provide a written timeline for irreversible deletion in the plan.

- SCCs & addenda: we operate under the EU SCCs. For additional contractual language around operator access we typically propose a small addendum (we can share a redline).

Attached is an operator access matrix (CSV) that maps access categories to approval gates and logging artifacts.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Product Security Lead, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.com

Hi Maria / PharmaSys team,

Thanks — attaching the implementation plan and the operator access matrix for your review 
(attachments below). Short answers inline to your numbered items: 

1) Attestation: we will provide a signed attestation stating that under normal operations no personal data will be exported outside the EU for the agreed deployment configuration. Any exceptional access outside the EU requires documented approval (break-glass) and is logged; we will describe the escalation chain explicitly in the attestation.

2) Subprocessors: the current subprocessor list is included in the implementation plan. No subprocessor contract permits wholesale transfer outside the EU for in-region deployments; any DR/replication outside EU would require explicit written consent.

3) SCCs & addendum: attached is a draft addendum focused on operator access that we typically present to customers. Please review and propose edits; we can produce a redline within 48 hours of receiving PharmaSys legal comments.
